notes: William R. King was elected vice president with 254 electoral votes to William Alexander Graham’s 42.
The South Carolina legislature chose the state’s electors. Every other state chose its electors by statewide popular vote.

The votes under “Others” went to minor tickets, which Wikipedia’s national table lists as Daniel Webster (Union Whig) 7,378, Jacob Broom (Native American) 2,415, George Troup (Southern Rights) 2,205 and William Goodell (Liberty Party) 72.
In Georgia a second slate of Pierce electors, the Union Democrats’, won 5,804 votes. They are counted in Pierce’s total, as Georgia’s two rival Jackson slates are in 1828.
